title: Universal Life Insurance Rider Service Standard: The Overloan Protection Charge
content:
## Standard

When an approved overloan protection election on an Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance policy is carried out, a one-time overloan protection charge is deducted from the account value and booked in the policy's activity history. The charge entry, dated the day it is booked, is what the account value is reduced by when the rider is carried out.

## Charge basis

The overloan protection charge is figured only after the policy's loan interest paid-to date stands at the date the charge is figured, so that no loan interest is left accruing from an earlier date.

Put the other way: while the loan interest paid-to date shown on the policy is earlier than the date the charge is figured, the charge is not figured.

| Loan interest paid-to date on the policy | Overloan protection charge |
|---|---|
| The date the charge is figured | This condition is met |
| An earlier date | Not figured |

## Charge booking tool: `assess_overloan_charge_72382565`

**Capability.** Books the one-time overloan protection charge on an Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance policy. One call adds one overloan protection charge entry, dated today, to the policy's activity history with the charge as given. Nothing else on the policy changes.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `ul_policy_id` | The reference number of the universal life policy the charge is booked on, read from the universal life policy lookup | Identifier, as recorded |
| `overloan_charge` | The overloan protection charge to deduct | USD, 2 decimal places, rounded half-up to the cent; greater than zero |

**Return.** A dictionary rendered as text with `ul_txn_id` (the reference number of the charge entry), `ul_policy_id` (the policy), `overloan_charge` (the charge booked, USD with 2 decimal places), `transaction_date` (today, YYYY-MM-DD) and `status`, which reads `charge_booked` when the entry was added. No other return is defined.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A policy whose loan interest paid-to date reads 3 September, on which the charge would be figured on 3 September, meets the charge basis; the same policy with a paid-to date of 14 June does not, the paid-to date being earlier than the date the charge is figured.
